info.title: MarketBox 2.0 Open API
info.description: The MarketBox public API for building booking experiences. Core model: create an order, then draw its order items down into bookings. Single bookings reference an order item per service line; package bookings draw one PACKAGE item down across N sessions. To schedule a package, build a slate (POST /availability/package-slate) and book it by slateId (POST /orders/{orderId}/package-bookings). See the guides for end-to-end walkthroughs.

ApiKeyAuth.name: x-api-key
ApiKeyAuth.description: API key minted in the MarketBox dashboard. Scope is restricted to the projects you select at creation time.

post.summary: Create a new booking
post.description: Creates a single booking. Each service line must reference an existing order + order item (orderId + orderItemId) to draw down — create and pay for an order first. Location fields depend on locationType: TRAVEL_ZONE requires locationId, latitude, longitude, and a structured address; PHYSICAL requires only locationId; VIRTUAL requires none. Local-time fields are derived server-side from bookingTz and must not be sent.

longitude.description: Client longitude. Required for TRAVEL_ZONE; must be omitted for PHYSICAL/VIRTUAL.

address.description: Structured client address. Required for TRAVEL_ZONE bookings.

businessModelType.description: How the service is sold (e.g. SINGLE_BOOKING).

orderItemId.description: The specific order item (SINGLE_SESSION) to draw down.

services.description: One line per service booked; each draws down an order item.

post.summary: Create a new order
post.description: Creates an order (a cart/purchase record). For a package, add an item with { skuType: "PACKAGE", packageId } — the server derives service, offering, session count (creditCount), price and expiry from the package. For a single session use { skuType: "SINGLE_SESSION", serviceId, offeringId, quantity }. The order item is the credit ledger: its quantityRemaining is what bookings draw down. Currency is fixed at creation.

post.summary: Create N package sessions atomically (or best-effort) from one PACKAGE order item
post.description: Books all sessions of a package against one PACKAGE order item. Provide exactly one source: slateId (book a whole slate — recommended; the server resolves times/supplier/location and fills the travel-zone location itself), slotIds (cherry-pick), or sessions (explicit). Booking does NOT require the order to be paid — credits exist from order creation. Note: this response is NOT wrapped in a { data } envelope, and created[].sessionIndex is 0-based. Returns 409 with freshSuggestions if a chosen slot went stale, or with code SLOT_HELD/SLOT_BOOKED naming the blocking claim if the requested time is taken.

orderItemId.description: The PACKAGE order item to draw down. All N sessions decrement its quantityRemaining.

idempotencyKey.description: Idempotency key that makes retry attempts safe; reusing it returns the original result.

atomicity.description: all_or_nothing (default, one transaction, max 15 sessions) or best_effort (per-session; requires project opt-in).

sessions.description: Explicit, client-supplied sessions (advanced). Prefer slateId. Provide exactly one of sessions, slateId, or slotIds.

slateId.description: Book an entire persisted slate by id (recommended). The server resolves every session; send no session details.

slotIds.description: Cherry-pick specific persisted slots by id. Provide exactly one of sessions, slateId, or slotIds.

created.description: Bookings created, each with a 0-based sessionIndex, bookingId and allocationId.

quantityRemaining.description: Credits left on the order item after this call.

post.summary: Supplier-centric availability: paginated suppliers, each with open slots grouped by day
post.description: Returns availability grouped by supplier — a paginated list of suppliers, each with its full profile (same shape as GET /suppliers) and its open slots bucketed by local day. Use this to render a wall of supplier cards with bookable times, instead of the flat, slot-centric arrays /availability/search returns. Provide serviceId + offeringId and either locationId or both lat and lng. Returns regular-interval open slots only — no clustered/travel-optimized suggestions and no recurring patterns (use /availability/search for those). Suppliers that match the service and location but have no availability in the window are still returned, with days: []. Paginate with limit (max 50) + the opaque cursor; nextCursor is null on the last page. Each slot carries a UTC anchor (startUtc/endUtc) plus *Local strings rendered in the request timezone.

serviceId.description: The service to find supplier availability for.

offeringId.description: The specific offering (variant) of the service being booked.

locationId.description: Where the service is delivered. Provide this OR both `lat` and `lng`. A stored location id (PHYSICAL / VIRTUAL / TRAVEL_ZONE).

lat.description: Client/service latitude. Provide `lat` + `lng` together as an alternative to `locationId` (in-home / travel-zone discovery).

durationMinutes.description: Override the booked duration (minutes). Only honoured for FLEXIBLE offerings; otherwise the offering’s own duration is used.

lookAheadStartDate.description: Start of the search window (ISO-8601). Defaults to now. Slots before this instant are excluded.

lookAheadDays.description: How many days forward to search from the start. Defaults to the engine’s configured window.

timezone.description: IANA timezone governing day bucketing and every `*Local` field in the response. Defaults to the project timezone.

interval.description: Open-slot granularity in minutes (e.g. 15 → :00 / :15 / :30 / :45). Defaults to 15.

language.description: Preferred language for supplier/service matching in multilingual projects.

limit.description: Suppliers per page (1–50, default 20). Kept small because each supplier’s availability is computed on demand.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination token from a previous response’s `nextCursor`. Omit for the first page.

200.description: Suppliers, each with open slots grouped by day

supplier.description: The supplier, in the same enriched shape as `GET /suppliers` (profile, `avatarUrl`, `services`, `skills`, `locations`) — enough to render a card without a follow-up call.

date.description: Local calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD) in the request `timezone` — the day these slots fall on.

slotId.description: Opaque id for this open slot. A slot is availability, not a hold — book it with the times below; it can be taken by another client until you do.

startUtc.description: Slot start as a UTC instant (ISO-8601, Z). Use this as the booking start anchor.

startLocal.description: Slot start rendered in the request `timezone` (ISO-8601 with numeric offset). For display.

endUtc.description: Slot end (start + the resolved service duration) as a UTC instant.

endLocal.description: Slot end rendered in the request `timezone`. For display.

days.description: Days with open slots, ascending. Empty (`[]`) when this supplier matches the service and location but has no availability in the window.

data.description: Suppliers on this page, in a stable order across pages.

timezone.description: The IANA timezone used for day bucketing and every `*Local` field (the request `timezone`, or the project default).

post.summary: Build a single-supplier N-session package slate (policy-driven), persisting suggestions
post.description: Builds one or more "slates" — complete N-session plans for a package — from a single supplier's availability. Pass packageId (session count is derived from its creditCount), a location (locationId, or lat+lng+address for travel zones), a timezone, a lookAheadStartDate with a numeric offset, and an rrule with a bounded COUNT. When persist is true (default) the returned primarySlate.slateId can be booked directly via POST /orders/{orderId}/package-bookings with { slateId }. Returns 422 when nothing is bookable.

packageId.description: The package to plan sessions for. serviceId, offeringId and the session count (creditCount) are resolved from it server-side.

locationId.description: Discovery by a stored location id. Provide this OR lat+lng.

lat.description: Client latitude (travel-zone branch). Provide with lng instead of locationId.

address.description: Structured client address. Required on the lat/lng (travel-zone) branch — it is stamped onto every returned slot so a later book-by-id satisfies the TRAVEL_ZONE address rule.

supplierId.description: Pin the plan to one supplier; only that supplier is considered.

lookAheadStartDate.description: When the recurring window starts. MUST carry a numeric UTC offset (e.g. -04:00), NOT a Z suffix.

rrule.description: Cadence for the sessions. MUST include a bounded, positive COUNT.

maxAlternates.description: Max runner-up (alternate supplier) slates to return.

persist.description: Persist the slate so it can be booked later by slateId. Defaults true.

post.summary: List a service's packages, each with a ready-to-book slate
post.description: Returns every ACTIVE package of a service, each with a complete N-session plan built from a supplier's real availability. The response entry carries a slateId that can be booked directly via POST /orders/{orderId}/package-bookings. Cadence defaults to FREQ=WEEKLY;COUNT={creditCount}, derived per package. Packages that cannot be planned come back with status NO_COMPLETE_SLATE or NO_AVAILABILITY and a reason — they do not fail the request.

post.summary: Hold supplier time during checkout — a single session, or a whole package slate
post.description: Claims supplier time so nobody else can book it while your customer pays. Provide exactly one of: intervals (explicit supplier time — this is the form that works for a SINGLE session, with no package and no slate), slateId (hold every slot of a persisted package slate), or slotIds (cherry-pick slots of a slate). Every interval is claimed in ONE transaction, so a hold is all-or-nothing — you never end up holding 3 sessions of a 5-session package. Expiry is LAZY: nothing runs at heldUntil, the hold simply stops blocking, so convert before then. To HEARTBEAT a checkout page, re-post the same intervals AND the reservationId you were given (with the same heldBy): that EXTENDS the existing hold — heldUntil moves out, the same reservationId comes back, and no second hold is minted. Omitting reservationId always mints a NEW hold. Returns 409 with code SLOT_HELD/SLOT_BOOKED — naming the blocking reservationId or bookingId — when the time is already claimed, or RESERVATION_NOT_FOUND / RESERVATION_NOT_HELD / RESERVATION_FORBIDDEN when the reservationId you asked to extend is unknown, no longer held, or not yours.

The intervals you send must be the ones that hold already claims, and heldBy must match the hold's owner. A mismatch is 409 RESERVATION_FORBIDDEN; an unknown id is 409 RESERVATION_NOT_FOUND; an already converted/released hold is 409 RESERVATION_NOT_HELD. Omit this field to mint a NEW hold.

post.summary: Convert a hold into confirmed bookings (the idempotent purchase hook)
post.description: Turns the held supplier time into real bookings, drawing credits from the given order item. The order item's skuType decides what is booked: a PACKAGE item books every held interval as package sessions; a SINGLE_SESSION item books the ONE held interval as an ordinary single booking — no package, and no 1-credit "reservation vehicle" package needed. (A SINGLE_SESSION item against a hold covering more than one interval returns 409 RESERVATION_MULTI_INTERVAL; any other skuType returns 400.) Call it from your payment webhook: it is idempotent on the reservationId (the package booking write uses the deterministic key convert:<reservationId>), so a webhook firing twice replays the same bookings rather than double-booking, and a reservation already CONVERTED replays its stored result. The bookings are rebuilt from the RESERVATION and the ORDER ITEM — never by re-resolving a suggestion that may have expired — so the booked service and the credit it draws down cannot disagree. Returns 409 HOLD_EXPIRED if you converted too late (the hold no longer blocks anyone), or SLOT_HELD/SLOT_BOOKED if someone else took the time in the meantime. This response is NOT wrapped in a { data } envelope, and created[].sessionIndex is 0-based.

atomicity.description: all_or_nothing (default) books every session in one transaction. best_effort requires suggestionConfig.allowPartialPackages.
